final_message:
DONE

I built a three-scenario recovery workbook and a written scenario summary. Only Scenario 3, the 10-hour shift with Grill Guard moved out, catches up and ships May's PO on time. I couldn't recalculate the workbook formulas here (no LibreOffice), so they will fill in when you open it in Excel.

| | Scenario 1: current capacity and cell | Scenario 2: Grill Guard moved out | Scenario 3: 10-hour shift, Grill Guard moved out |
|---|---|---|---|
| April PO in transit by Apr 13 | No: Crew Cab done Apr 25, Extended Cab done about May 9 | No: Crew Cab done Apr 9, Extended Cab done Apr 19 | Yes: done Apr 12, no spare day |
| May PO ships May 1 on time | No: nothing from May is produced by Apr 30 | No: Extended Cab May is 510 sets short at Apr 30, Crew Cab May just makes it | Yes: done Apr 27, one working day of spare |
| Sets outstanding at Apr 30 | 2,250 | 510 | 0 |

The workbook has a daily plan for each scenario in the same format, plus a comparison sheet and a sheet with the open PO data. Every plan shows each day's production, the open POs and a running tally against them. The summary document covers each scenario's actions, what it means for Crew Cab, Extended Cab and Grill Guard, and a pass/fail on May.

Things I assumed that you should check before the meeting:
- **Grill Guard run rate:** it wasn't provided, so Scenario 1 assumes the 100 units a week take one full cell-day each week (Fridays; Thursday Mar 29 for Good Friday). Scenario 2 has no Grill Guard impact at all and still fails, so Scenario 1's result doesn't depend on this.
- **Grill Guard move:** in Scenarios 2 and 3 the cell makes Grill Guards on Jan 26 only. The alternate cell takes over from Feb 2, since it's ready Feb 1.
- **10-hour window:** I ran it Feb 5 to Mar 2, to line up with the 135/day upgrade. The 30-day notice has to go out by Jan 5 for that start.
- **Holidays:** Louis Riel Day (Feb 19) and Good Friday (Mar 30) are non-production days. The 10-hour window includes Feb 19, so it has 19 production days at 170.
- **Shipping:** a PO ships the working day after its last unit is built. "In transit by Apr 13" therefore means April production done by Apr 12, and May done by Apr 30.
- **Source listing error:** its open-quantity total leaves out May, so I included May's 900 Crew Cab and 575 Extended Cab.

Scenario 3 has almost no slack. It has zero days on the April PO and one on May. A material slip after Jan 22, or larger March to May POs (those quantities are forecasts), would break it.

Files are in outputs/:
- Running_Board_Recovery_Plan.xlsx
- Running_Board_Scenario_Summary.docx
